modules.title: Explore the Iceberg data product
modules.question: What has the platform team published to us, and what can we (not) do with it?

steps.title: Open the payments-hol Workspace
steps.body: This shared Workspace is where you'll build every module. Take a quick tour: **Home** and the **+** button list everything you can create here (SQL file, Notebook, dbt Project, Streamlit App, Agent, Semantic view, Pipeline Builder). The file explorer on the left holds the lab project (`dbt/`, `vignettes/`). The bottom panel has Query History and, later, the dbt pane. Snowsight sometimes reopens **My Workspace**, so check the name top left whenever you come back.
steps.where: Snowsight > **Projects > Workspaces**, then the **My Workspace** dropdown (top left) > **payments-hol**
steps.expect: the payments-hol Workspace open, with `dbt/`, `notebooks/` and `vignettes/` in the file explorer

Start a new chat (**+** at the top of the sidebar) at the beginning of each module, so each one starts with a clean context. You're signed in as `HOL_PARTICIPANT` with the `BARCLAYS_WH` warehouse. Cortex Code still checks for a warehouse at the start of each chat, so each module page gives you a one-line context prompt to paste first. That saves it looking.

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- BARCLAYS PAYMENTS HOL v2 - SHARED CORE
-- C1: EXPLORE THE PUBLISHED ICEBERG DATA PRODUCT  (~25 min, all personas)
--
-- Business context: you are part of Payments Operations for Corporate
-- Banking. The platform team has published nine source tables to the
-- enterprise data platform as Iceberg tables. You can read them but you
-- cannot load or change them - exactly like Barclayflake.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA;

-- C1.1 What has been published to us?
SHOW ICEBERG TABLES IN SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA;
-- Note the catalog (SNOWFLAKE) and that storage is Snowflake-managed.
-- At Barclays the same tables sit on the bank's own object storage
-- via an external volume; the SQL you write is identical.

-- C1.2 Iceberg tables keep open metadata - this is what lets other engines
-- (Spark, Trino, etc.) read the same data with no copy.
SELECT SYSTEM$GET_ICEBERG_TABLE_INFORMATION('BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS') AS ICEBERG_METADATA;

-- C1.3 Prove the guard-rails: attendees cannot load or modify source data.
-- Expect: "Insufficient privileges". This is intentional.
-- INSERT INTO PAYMENTS (PAYMENT_ID) VALUES ('TEST');

-- C1.4 Get to know the data model (see docs/data_sources.md for the ERD)
SELECT 'PAYMENTS' AS TABLE_NAME, COUNT(*) AS ROW_COUNT FROM PAYMENTS
UNION ALL SELECT 'CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK',     COUNT(*) FROM CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK
UNION ALL SELECT 'OPERATIONAL_ALERTS',    COUNT(*) FROM OPERATIONAL_ALERTS
UNION ALL SELECT 'CUSTOMERS',             COUNT(*) FROM CUSTOMERS
UNION ALL SELECT 'ACCOUNTS',              COUNT(*) FROM ACCOUNTS
UNION ALL SELECT 'RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS', COUNT(*) FROM RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS
ORDER BY ROW_COUNT DESC;

-- C1.5 Payments mix by scheme - the six UK/international rails
SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE,
       COUNT(*)                                        AS PAYMENTS,
       ROUND(SUM(AMOUNT) / 1e6, 1)                     AS VOLUME_M,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'COMPLETED') / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT
FROM PAYMENTS
GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE
ORDER BY PAYMENTS DESC;

-- C1.6 A corporate client 360 in one query: customer -> RM -> accounts -> payments -> feedback
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR, r.RM_NAME, r.TEAM,
       COUNT(DISTINCT a.ACCOUNT_ID)                    AS ACCOUNTS,
       COUNT(DISTINCT p.PAYMENT_ID)                    AS PAYMENTS,
       COUNT(DISTINCT IFF(p.STATUS = 'FAILED', p.PAYMENT_ID, NULL)) AS FAILED,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.FEEDBACK_ID)                   AS FEEDBACK_ITEMS
FROM CUSTOMERS c
JOIN RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS r ON c.RM_ID = r.RM_ID
JOIN ACCOUNTS a              ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN PAYMENTS p         ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK f ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY FAILED DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- C1.7 Iceberg time travel works too: what did PAYMENTS look like an hour ago?
-- (Uncomment once the tables are at least a few minutes old.)
-- SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PAYMENTS AT (OFFSET => -60*5);

-- C1.8 Ask Cortex Code (CoCo panel in your Workspace):
--   "Describe the tables in BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA and how they join together."
--   "Which customers have the highest payment failure rate? Write the SQL and run it."

SELECT 'Core C1 complete - pick your pathway in pathways/' AS STATUS;

modules.title: Iceberg + dbt pipeline with Cortex Code
modules.question: Turn the published Iceberg sources into governed, tested data products - and publish them back to the lake as Iceberg.
build: The dbt project in the Workspace (4 staging views, 2 marts, pre-written tests), run from the Workspace dbt pane
Two Cortex Code-built marts: `mart_customer_payments`, `mart_rm_performance`
Nightly task `TSK_DBT_NIGHTLY_BUILD` (suspended)
Iceberg data product `DP_SLA_COMPLIANCE`

steps.title: Publish the data product back to the lake as Iceberg
steps.prompt: Create a Snowflake-managed Iceberg table BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.DP_SLA_COMPLIANCE (CATALOG = 'SNOWFLAKE') from MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE, casting PAYMENT_DAY to TIMESTAMP_NTZ(6) because Iceberg stores microseconds. Add a comment describing it as a data product, then show its Iceberg metadata location.
steps.expect: `DP_SLA_COMPLIANCE` listed by `SHOW ICEBERG TABLES IN SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS`, with a metadata location other engines can read

modules.note: Production Iceberg tables use the bank's external volume (one volume, one IAM role across accounts) rather than Snowflake-managed storage. dbt models and SQL are otherwise identical.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DE1: ICEBERG + dbt PIPELINE WITH CORTEX CODE   (~60 min)
-- Persona: Data Engineer
-- Question: "Turn the published Iceberg sources into governed, tested
--            data products - and publish them back to the lake as Iceberg."
-- Prereq:   Core C1 only. (Produces everything core_analytics.sql would.)
--
-- Work in the lab Workspace payments-hol (Projects > Workspaces > My Workspace dropdown), which is
-- already in your account. On your own account, create one from
-- https://github.com/sfc-gh-boconnor/payments-hol (Projects > Workspaces >
-- From Git repository).
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE1.1 Walk the dbt project (Workspace file explorer: dbt/)
--   models/staging/schema.yml  - sources point at BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA (Iceberg)
--   models/staging/*.sql       - 4 views: cast, clean, denormalise
--   models/marts/*.sql         - mart_payment_kpis, mart_sla_compliance
--   macros/generate_schema_name.sql - land models in ANALYTICS, not ANALYTICS_ANALYTICS
-- dbt reads Iceberg sources exactly like native tables. No code changes.
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE1.2 Deploy and run as a dbt Project on Snowflake
-- In the Workspace: open the dbt tab in the bottom panel, choose build from the
-- Run dropdown and run it.
-- Or from SQL / a task (this is how you would schedule it in production):
-- -----------------------------------------------------
EXECUTE DBT PROJECT BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.BARCLAYS_DBT ARGS = 'build';
-- Expect: Done. PASS=27 WARN=0 ERROR=0

-- Schedule it - one task, no external orchestrator
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK TSK_DBT_NIGHTLY_BUILD
    WAREHOUSE = BARCLAYS_WH
    SCHEDULE  = 'USING CRON 0 5 * * * Europe/London'
AS
    EXECUTE DBT PROJECT BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.BARCLAYS_DBT ARGS = 'build';
-- Left suspended for the lab. In production: ALTER TASK TSK_DBT_NIGHTLY_BUILD RESUME;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE1.3 Accelerate with Cortex Code (CoCo panel in the Workspace)
-- Prompt 1:
--   "Create a dbt mart model mart_customer_payments in dbt/models/marts that
--    summarises payment activity per customer: total payments, total volume,
--    success rate and most-used payment scheme. Join stg_payments -> stg_accounts
--    -> stg_customers and follow the patterns in mart_payment_kpis.sql."
-- Prompt 2:
--   "Create mart_rm_performance: one row per relationship manager with rm_id,
--    rm_name, client_count, total volume, average success rate and their client
--    with the lowest success rate. Then run dbt build and fix any failing tests."
-- The tests for both models already exist in models/marts/schema.yml, so
-- `dbt build` proves CoCo's code is correct.
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE1.4 Validate
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT 'STG_PAYMENTS' AS OBJ, COUNT(*) AS ROWS_ FROM STG_PAYMENTS
UNION ALL SELECT 'MART_PAYMENT_KPIS',   COUNT(*) FROM MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
UNION ALL SELECT 'MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE', COUNT(*) FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE;

SELECT SLA_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS SCHEME_DAYS
FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE GROUP BY SLA_STATUS ORDER BY SCHEME_DAYS DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE1.5 Publish the data product back to the lake as Iceberg
-- Consumers on other engines (Spark, Trino, etc.) can now read the mart with no copy.
-- Iceberg stores microsecond precision, so timestamps are cast to scale 6.
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE ICEBERG TABLE DP_SLA_COMPLIANCE
    CATALOG = 'SNOWFLAKE'
    COMMENT = 'Data product: daily SLA compliance per payment scheme (Iceberg)'
AS SELECT * REPLACE (PAYMENT_DAY::TIMESTAMP_NTZ(6) AS PAYMENT_DAY)
   FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE;

SELECT SYSTEM$GET_ICEBERG_TABLE_INFORMATION('BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.DP_SLA_COMPLIANCE') AS METADATA_LOCATION;

-- Barclayflake note: in production the Iceberg table would use the bank's
-- EXTERNAL_VOLUME (one volume and one IAM role, shared across accounts)
-- instead of Snowflake-managed storage. The SQL above is otherwise unchanged.

SELECT 'DE1 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DE2: DYNAMIC TABLES + DATA QUALITY   (~45 min)
-- Persona: Data Engineer
-- Question: "How do I keep an ops-floor SLA monitor fresh without writing
--            orchestration, and prove the data feeding it is trustworthy?"
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql  (or DE1 + DA2)
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE2.1 Dynamic Tables: declare the result, Snowflake keeps it fresh
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- Ops-floor SLA breach monitor: never more than 1 minute stale
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_LIVE_SLA_BREACHES
    TARGET_LAG = '1 minute'
    WAREHOUSE  = BARCLAYS_WH
AS
SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE,
       SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS)  AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(FAILED_PAYMENTS) AS BREACHED_PAYMENTS,
       ROUND(SUM(FAILED_PAYMENTS)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS BREACH_RATE_PCT,
       MIN(PAYMENT_DAY) AS EARLIEST_BREACH,
       MAX(PAYMENT_DAY) AS LATEST_BREACH
FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE
WHERE SLA_STATUS = 'BREACH'
GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE;

-- Failed-payment triage feed built straight off the Iceberg source.
-- Dynamic tables can read Iceberg tables directly - no copy into Snowflake storage.
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_FAILED_PAYMENT_TRIAGE
    TARGET_LAG = DOWNSTREAM
    WAREHOUSE  = BARCLAYS_WH
AS
SELECT p.PAYMENT_ID, p.PAYMENT_DATE, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.AMOUNT, p.CURRENCY,
       p.ERROR_CODE, e.ERROR_DESCRIPTION, e.ERROR_CATEGORY, e.IS_RETRYABLE,
       c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR, r.RM_NAME
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS p
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ERROR_CODES e  ON p.ERROR_CODE = e.ERROR_CODE
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a     ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c    ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS r ON c.RM_ID = r.RM_ID
WHERE p.STATUS IN ('FAILED', 'RETURNED');

-- Downstream summary chained off the triage feed
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_RETRYABLE_SUMMARY
    TARGET_LAG = '5 minutes'
    WAREHOUSE  = BARCLAYS_WH
AS
SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE, ERROR_CATEGORY, IS_RETRYABLE,
       COUNT(*) AS PAYMENTS, ROUND(SUM(AMOUNT), 2) AS VALUE_AT_RISK
FROM DT_FAILED_PAYMENT_TRIAGE
GROUP BY ALL;

SHOW DYNAMIC TABLES IN SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- Refresh history and the pipeline graph are also visible in Snowsight:
-- Monitoring > Dynamic Tables > DT_RETRYABLE_SUMMARY > Graph
SELECT NAME, STATE, REFRESH_ACTION, REFRESH_TRIGGER, DATA_TIMESTAMP
FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.DYNAMIC_TABLE_REFRESH_HISTORY())
WHERE NAME LIKE 'DT_%'
ORDER BY DATA_TIMESTAMP DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE2.2 Data Metric Functions: quality checks that run on a schedule
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- Schedule is set per table; changes also trigger a check
ALTER TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS SET DATA_METRIC_SCHEDULE = 'TRIGGER_ON_CHANGES';

-- System DMFs
ALTER TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS ADD DATA METRIC FUNCTION
    SNOWFLAKE.CORE.NULL_COUNT ON (RM_NAME);
ALTER TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS ADD DATA METRIC FUNCTION
    SNOWFLAKE.CORE.DUPLICATE_COUNT ON (CUSTOMER_ID);

-- A custom, business-rule DMF: success rate must be a valid percentage
-- (the argument type must match the column type - SUCCESS_RATE_PCT is FLOAT)
CREATE OR REPLACE DATA METRIC FUNCTION INVALID_SUCCESS_RATE_COUNT(
    t TABLE (SUCCESS_RATE_PCT FLOAT))
RETURNS NUMBER
AS
$$
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t
    WHERE SUCCESS_RATE_PCT IS NULL OR SUCCESS_RATE_PCT < 0 OR SUCCESS_RATE_PCT > 100
$$;

ALTER TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS ADD DATA METRIC FUNCTION
    INVALID_SUCCESS_RATE_COUNT ON (SUCCESS_RATE_PCT);

-- Expectations: turn a metric into a pass/fail rule
ALTER TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS MODIFY DATA METRIC FUNCTION
    SNOWFLAKE.CORE.DUPLICATE_COUNT ON (CUSTOMER_ID)
    ADD EXPECTATION NO_DUPLICATE_CUSTOMERS (VALUE = 0);

-- Which checks are attached?
SELECT METRIC_NAME, REF_ARGUMENTS, SCHEDULE, SCHEDULE_STATUS
FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.DATA_METRIC_FUNCTION_REFERENCES(
    REF_ENTITY_NAME   => 'BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS',
    REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE'));

-- Run the checks on demand (scheduled results land in
-- SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.DATA_QUALITY_MONITORING_RESULTS after a few minutes)
SELECT SNOWFLAKE.CORE.NULL_COUNT(SELECT RM_NAME FROM MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS)        AS NULL_RM_NAMES,
       SNOWFLAKE.CORE.DUPLICATE_COUNT(SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS) AS DUPLICATE_CUSTOMERS,
       INVALID_SUCCESS_RATE_COUNT(SELECT SUCCESS_RATE_PCT FROM MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS) AS INVALID_RATES;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DE2.3 Cortex Code prompts (try in the CoCo panel)
-- -----------------------------------------------------

--   failed CHAPS payments over 1m GBP with the customer and RM, refreshing every
--   2 minutes. Then show me its refresh history."
--  "Add a data metric function to MART_PAYMENT_KPIS that counts rows where
--   P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS is less than AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS, and attach it."

SELECT 'DE2 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.title: Real-time payments: stream, mirror, serve, act
modules.prerequisites: C1 only. Uses `BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME`, the shared interactive warehouse `HOL_INTERACTIVE_WH`, and grants to create a Snowflake Postgres instance and mirror it (all set up at provisioning)
modules.question: A corporate client's payments are failing right now. How does the operations floor see it within seconds, not after tonight's dbt build, and serve that view to everyone watching at once?
build: A **Snowflake Postgres** instance `HOL_PAYMENTS_PG`: the operational payments database the payment engine writes to
A live feed of payment events into Postgres, with an incident hidden in the stream
A **Data Mirror** that streams every change from Postgres into **Snowflake-managed Iceberg** tables in `PAYMENTS_MIRROR`, with `$live` (seconds behind) and `$changes` (the change feed)
Ops-floor queries served from the **interactive warehouse** `HOL_INTERACTIVE_WH`, straight off the mirrored table
Dynamic table `DT_PAYMENT_INCIDENTS` that flags failing payment clusters within a minute

steps.title: Open the DE3 starter notebook
steps.body: Open the starter notebook `de3_realtime_payments`: it has the title and one numbered heading per step, so Cortex Code puts each cell in the right place. If you can't see the `notebooks/` and `vignettes/` folders in the file explorer, you're in the wrong Workspace: switch to **payments-hol** from the Workspace dropdown (top left) before you go on. (No starter? Use **+ > Notebook** in payments-hol and name it `de3_realtime_payments`.) Choose the compute pool **NOTEBOOK_POOL** and the warehouse **BARCLAYS_WH**, and check the role is **HOL_PARTICIPANT**. Open the notebook's settings (**⋮** > **Notebook settings** > **External access**) and turn on **HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION**: the notebook installs the Postgres driver from PyPI and connects to Postgres on port 5432.
steps.where: the **payments-hol** Workspace (not My Workspace) > file explorer > `notebooks/de3_realtime_payments.ipynb`
steps.expect: the starter notebook open in payments-hol with its numbered headings, a connected kernel and the external access integration enabled

steps.title: Create the Postgres instance

steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `de3_realtime_payments` open

Under heading 1, add a Python cell named create_pg that runs !pip install psycopg2-binary, makes vignettes/de3_realtime_payments/de3_postgres.py importable (search upwards from the current working directory for a folder containing vignettes/de3_realtime_payments/de3_postgres.py and add that folder to sys.path), imports de3_postgres as pg, and runs host = pg.create_postgres(get_active_session()). Don't rewrite the helper and never print the password. Then add a markdown cell explaining what create_postgres does: the instance size and why, the network policy, and what happens to the one-time password.
steps.expect: the cell prints the instance moving through CREATING, STARTING and FINALIZING, then returns its host after 3 to 5 minutes. `HOL_PAYMENTS_PG` uses `STANDARD_M`, the smallest size Data Mirroring supports, with the network policy `HOL_PG_POLICY`. Its `snowflake_admin` password is shown only once, in the CREATE result, so the helper saves it straight into the secret `BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME.PG_ADMIN_SECRET` without printing it.

steps.title: Reveal the connection and connect
steps.body: Click **Reveal Postgres connection**: it reads the secret and shows the host, user and password with copy buttons. Paste them into a new Python cell under heading 2: ```python PG_HOST = "<host>" PG_USER = "snowflake_admin" PG_PASS = "<password>" ``` Run it, then paste this into the Cortex Code sidebar:
steps.where: the Lab Companion > **DE3** > **Reveal Postgres connection**, then the notebook
steps.prompt: Under heading 2, after my connection cell, add a Python cell named source_table that opens conn = pg.connect(PG_HOST, PG_USER, PG_PASS) and runs pg.create_source_table(conn), printing the row count it returns. Then explain the table it created in Postgres and why it has a primary key.
steps.expect: `0` rows in the new Postgres table `payments.payment_events`. The primary key lets the mirror carry updates and deletes as well as inserts. Keep the password out of anything you share. You can reveal it again any time, for example after a kernel restart. If the Lab Companion says the password wasn't saved, run `pg.reset_password(get_active_session())` and reveal again.

steps.title: Mirror Postgres into Snowflake
steps.prompt: Under heading 3, add a Python cell named mirror that runs pg.start_mirror(get_active_session()) and shows the result as a table. Then add a markdown cell explaining Snowflake Postgres Data Mirroring: what CREATE_MIRROR creates in PAYMENTS_MIRROR (an Iceberg table plus $live and $changes), who owns it, and what refresh_interval means.
steps.expect: `payments.payment_events` in state `REPLICATING` in the new database `PAYMENTS_MIRROR`. The mirror owns `PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS`, a Snowflake-managed Iceberg table in open Parquet, plus `PAYMENT_EVENTS$live` (the table plus changes not merged yet, so it's seconds behind) and `PAYMENT_EVENTS$changes` (the change feed). Changes merge into the base table every minute (`refresh_interval`). Nothing to schedule or run: the mirror keeps going on its own.

steps.title: Stream payments into Postgres
steps.prompt: Under heading 4, add a Python cell named stream that runs pg.stream_payments(conn, get_active_session()) to insert about 20 payment events a second into Postgres for 5 minutes, and prints the total it returns. Then explain in a markdown cell what the stream sends, including the SEPA incident in the second half.
steps.expect: the cell runs for 5 minutes, printing progress every 30 seconds, and sends about 6,000 events. While it runs, open a SQL worksheet and run `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS$live` a few times: the count climbs about 20 to 40 seconds behind Postgres. Halfway through, one corporate client's SEPA payments start failing with "Beneficiary bank unavailable".

steps.title: Measure how fresh the data is
steps.prompt: Under heading 5, add a SQL cell named freshness: events and failed events per minute for the last 15 minutes from PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS$live, then the seconds between the newest EVENT_TS and SYSDATE() in both PAYMENT_EVENTS$live and the base table PAYMENT_EVENTS, then the count of rows per _CHANGE_TYPE in PAYMENT_EVENTS$changes. Run it and explain what the numbers say about end-to-end latency from Postgres to Snowflake.
steps.expect: about 1,200 events a minute while streaming, with `$live` about 20 to 40 seconds behind and the base table up to a minute behind (its refresh interval). Failures jump in the second half: that's the incident. `$changes` shows one `I` (insert) per event; an update would appear as a `D` and an `I`.

steps.title: Serve the ops floor from the interactive warehouse
steps.prompt: Under heading 6, add a SQL cell named ops_floor that runs USE WAREHOUSE HOL_INTERACTIVE_WH, then the queries a payments operations dashboard would refresh every few seconds directly on PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS: failed payments and failed value by scheme in the last 15 minutes, and the 10 clients with the most failed value in the last 15 minutes joined to BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS for the name. Then switch back with USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH. Run it and explain zero-copy interactive analytics on an Iceberg table: why there's no copy or conversion, and when the 5 second statement limit matters.
steps.expect: answers from `HOL_INTERACTIVE_WH` in well under a second once it's warm, straight off the mirrored Iceberg table, with no copy. SEPA stands out, and one client has a cluster of failed SEPA payments. On a few thousand rows a standard warehouse is quick too: the interactive warehouse earns its keep when hundreds of screens, APIs or agents run these queries every few seconds at once. Heavy one-off analysis belongs on a standard warehouse, and DML is rejected, which is why the cell switches back.

steps.title: Flag incidents automatically
steps.prompt: Under heading 7, add a SQL cell named incidents that creates the dynamic table BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME.DT_PAYMENT_INCIDENTS with TARGET_LAG '1 minute' on warehouse BARCLAYS_WH: failed payments in PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS from the last 15 minutes grouped by CUSTOMER_ID (with CUSTOMER_NAME from BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS), SCHEME and FAILURE_REASON, with the failed count, failed value, first and last failure, keeping groups with at least 5 failures. Then query it, largest first, and draft the message the operations team would send to the client's relationship manager.
steps.expect: one incident: Crown Logistics' SEPA payments failing with "Beneficiary bank unavailable", with the count, value and time window. The table refreshes every minute on its own, so the moment a new cluster starts in Postgres, it appears here. This is the same pattern as DE2's live SLA breaches, now on data streaming out of an operational database. Cortex Code automations (GOV2) could post it to the ops team.

-- =====================================================
-- DE3: Real-time payments - reference SQL
-- The Postgres side is Python (de3_postgres.py); this is the Snowflake SQL around it.
-- Flow: Snowflake Postgres HOL_PAYMENTS_PG -> Data Mirror -> Snowflake-managed Iceberg
--       PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS (+ $live, $changes) -> interactive warehouse, dynamic table
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- 1. The instance (create_postgres runs the CREATE and saves the one-time password in the secret):
--    CREATE POSTGRES INSTANCE HOL_PAYMENTS_PG COMPUTE_FAMILY = 'STANDARD_M' STORAGE_SIZE_GB = 10
--      AUTHENTICATION_AUTHORITY = POSTGRES POSTGRES_VERSION = 18 NETWORK_POLICY = 'HOL_PG_POLICY';
SHOW POSTGRES INSTANCES LIKE 'HOL_PAYMENTS_PG';
DESCRIBE SECRET BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME.PG_ADMIN_SECRET;   -- metadata only: the password isn't shown

-- 2. The mirror (start_mirror runs these)
GRANT USAGE ON POSTGRES INSTANCE HOL_PAYMENTS_PG TO APPLICATION SNOWFLAKE;
-- CALL SNOWFLAKE.POSTGRES.CREATE_MIRROR(
--     mirror_name => 'payments_mirror', postgres_instance => 'HOL_PAYMENTS_PG', postgres_database => 'postgres',
--     target_database => 'PAYMENTS_MIRROR', postgres_schemas => ['payments'],
--     refresh_interval => '1 minute', target_table_type => 'ICEBERG');
SELECT * FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.POSTGRES.LIST_MIRRORS());
CALL SNOWFLAKE.POSTGRES.LIST_MIRRORED_TABLES('payments_mirror');
SHOW TABLES IN DATABASE PAYMENTS_MIRROR;   -- PAYMENT_EVENTS (Iceberg) and PAYMENT_EVENTS$CHANGES, owned by the mirror

-- 3. Freshness: volume and failures per minute, and how far each view is behind
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('minute', EVENT_TS) AS MINUTE, COUNT(*) AS EVENTS, COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'FAILED') AS FAILED
FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS$live
WHERE EVENT_TS >= DATEADD('minute', -15, SYSDATE())
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT 'live' AS VIEW_NAME, DATEDIFF('second', MAX(EVENT_TS), SYSDATE()) AS SECONDS_BEHIND FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS$live
UNION ALL
SELECT 'base Iceberg table', DATEDIFF('second', MAX(EVENT_TS), SYSDATE()) FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS;

-- The change feed: I = insert, D = delete (an update is a D plus an I)
SELECT _CHANGE_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CHANGES FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS$changes GROUP BY 1;

-- 4. Ops floor on the shared interactive warehouse: zero-copy, straight off the mirrored Iceberg table
USE WAREHOUSE HOL_INTERACTIVE_WH;

SELECT SCHEME, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' AND EVENT_TS >= DATEADD('minute', -15, SYSDATE())
GROUP BY SCHEME
ORDER BY FAILED_VALUE DESC;

SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, e.SCHEME, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS, SUM(e.AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS e
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = e.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE e.STATUS = 'FAILED' AND e.EVENT_TS >= DATEADD('minute', -15, SYSDATE())
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY FAILED_VALUE DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Interactive warehouses reject DML and procedures: switch back before creating anything
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- 5. Incidents: failing clusters in the last 15 minutes, refreshed every minute
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME.DT_PAYMENT_INCIDENTS
  TARGET_LAG = '1 minute'
  WAREHOUSE = BARCLAYS_WH
  COMMENT = 'DE3: failing payment clusters in the last 15 minutes, refreshed every minute'
AS
SELECT e.CUSTOMER_ID,
       c.CUSTOMER_NAME,
       e.SCHEME,
       e.FAILURE_REASON,
       COUNT(*)         AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(e.AMOUNT)    AS FAILED_VALUE,
       MIN(e.EVENT_TS)  AS FIRST_FAILURE,
       MAX(e.EVENT_TS)  AS LAST_FAILURE
FROM PAYMENTS_MIRROR.PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_EVENTS e
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = e.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE e.STATUS = 'FAILED'
  AND e.EVENT_TS >= DATEADD('minute', -15, SYSDATE())
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

SELECT * FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.REALTIME.DT_PAYMENT_INCIDENTS ORDER BY FAILED_PAYMENTS DESC;

-- 6. After the lab: the instance bills while it runs
-- ALTER POSTGRES INSTANCE HOL_PAYMENTS_PG SUSPEND;
-- Facilitator teardown: CALL SNOWFLAKE.POSTGRES.DROP_MIRROR(mirror_name => 'payments_mirror', drop_target_database => TRUE);
--                       DROP POSTGRES INSTANCE HOL_PAYMENTS_PG;

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA1: BUILD A SEMANTIC VIEW + ASK CORTEX ANALYST   (~60 min)
-- Persona: Data Analyst
-- Question: "Give RMs and ops a single, trusted definition of a corporate
--            client's payments health that anyone can query in plain English."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql  (STG_* views, FEEDBACK_ENRICHED)
-- Builds:   V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY, V_CLIENT_ALERTS, SV_CLIENT_360
-- (SV_PAYMENTS from the original lab is in setup/catchup/semantic_view_and_agent.sql
--  - open it and compare as a worked example.)
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.1 Stable interface views (semantic views should sit on contracts, not raw)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
    COMMENT = 'One row per corporate client: payment volumes, success and latency'
AS
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID,
       COUNT(*)                                                     AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_SUCCESSFUL)                                    AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_FAILED)                                        AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(p.AMOUNT)                                                AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
       SUM(IFF(p.IS_FAILED, p.AMOUNT, 0))                           AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
       ROUND(AVG(p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                          AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
       MAX(p.PAYMENT_DATE)                                          AS LAST_PAYMENT_DATE
FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_ALERTS
    COMMENT = 'Operational alerts attributed to the originating corporate client'
AS
SELECT al.ALERT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, al.ALERT_TIME::TIMESTAMP AS ALERT_TIME,
       al.SEVERITY, al.PAYMENT_TYPE, al.STATUS AS ALERT_STATUS,
       al.ASSIGNED_TO, al.RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN, al.ALERT_DESCRIPTION
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS p ON al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.2 The semantic view: business names, relationships, metrics, synonyms
-- Tip: you can also build this in Snowsight (AI & ML > Cortex Analyst > Create)
-- or ask CoCo: "Create a semantic view over STG_CUSTOMERS, V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY,
-- FEEDBACK_ENRICHED and V_CLIENT_ALERTS joined on CUSTOMER_ID."
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_CLIENT_360

  TABLES (
    clients AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('customers', 'corporate clients', 'accounts')
      COMMENT = 'Corporate banking clients with KYC status and assigned relationship manager',
    payments AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      COMMENT = 'Payment activity summary per client',
    feedback AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
      PRIMARY KEY (FEEDBACK_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('complaints', 'customer feedback', 'sentiment')
      COMMENT = 'Client feedback with AI sentiment and topic',
    alerts AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS
      PRIMARY KEY (ALERT_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('incidents', 'operational alerts')
      COMMENT = 'Operational payment alerts per client'
  )

  RELATIONSHIPS (
    payments_to_clients AS payments (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    feedback_to_clients AS feedback (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    alerts_to_clients   AS alerts   (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients
  )

  FACTS (
    payments.total_payments      AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.successful_payments AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.failed_payments     AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    payments.total_volume_gbp    AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
    payments.failed_volume_gbp   AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
    feedback.sentiment_score     AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
    feedback.rating              AS RATING,
    alerts.resolution_time_min   AS RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN
  )

  DIMENSIONS (
    clients.customer_name AS CUSTOMER_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('client', 'client name', 'company')
      COMMENT = 'Registered legal entity name (upper case)',
    clients.sector        AS SECTOR WITH SYNONYMS = ('industry'),
    clients.country       AS COUNTRY COMMENT = 'ISO alpha-3 country code',

    clients.rm_name       AS RM_NAME WITH SYNONYMS = ('relationship manager', 'RM', 'banker'),
    clients.rm_team       AS RM_TEAM COMMENT = 'Corporate, Institutional or SME banking team',
    feedback.sentiment_label AS SENTIMENT_LABEL COMMENT = 'POSITIVE, NEUTRAL, NEGATIVE',
    feedback.topic_category  AS TOPIC_CATEGORY,
    feedback.feedback_payment_type AS PAYMENT_TYPE COMMENT = 'Payment scheme the feedback refers to',
    feedback.feedback_date   AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    alerts.severity       AS SEVERITY COMMENT = 'LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL',
    alerts.alert_status   AS ALERT_STATUS COMMENT = 'OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGED, INVESTIGATING, RESOLVED',
    alerts.alert_time     AS ALERT_TIME
  )

  METRICS (
    payments.payment_count     AS SUM(payments.total_payments) WITH SYNONYMS = ('number of payments'),
    payments.payment_volume    AS SUM(payments.total_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('volume', 'value'),
    payments.failed_volume     AS SUM(payments.failed_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('value at risk'),
    payments.success_rate_pct  AS ROUND(SUM(payments.successful_payments) / NULLIF(SUM(payments.total_payments), 0) * 100, 2)
      COMMENT = 'Weighted payment success rate %',
    feedback.avg_sentiment     AS ROUND(AVG(feedback.sentiment_score), 3),
    feedback.negative_feedback_count AS COUNT_IF(feedback.sentiment_label = 'NEGATIVE'),
    alerts.open_alert_count    AS COUNT_IF(alerts.alert_status <> 'RESOLVED') WITH SYNONYMS = ('open incidents'),
    alerts.critical_alert_count AS COUNT_IF(alerts.severity = 'CRITICAL'),
    alerts.avg_resolution_min  AS ROUND(AVG(alerts.resolution_time_min), 0)
  )

  COMMENT = 'Corporate Client 360 for Payments Operations: payments health, feedback sentiment and operational alerts per client'

  AI_SQL_GENERATION 'Client names are stored in upper case; match them case-insensitively with ILIKE. Round percentages to 1 decimal place.'

  AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES (
    worst_clients AS (
      QUESTION 'Which 5 clients have the lowest payment success rate?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, ROUND(SUM(p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS) / NULLIF(SUM(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS success_rate_pct
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY p
           JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON p.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID

           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS a
           JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           GROUP BY c.RM_NAME ORDER BY open_alerts DESC'
    )
  );

SHOW SEMANTIC METRICS IN SV_CLIENT_360;

    SV_CLIENT_360
    DIMENSIONS clients.rm_name
    METRICS payments.payment_volume, payments.success_rate_pct, alerts.open_alert_count

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA2: AI SQL ON CUSTOMER FEEDBACK   (~45 min)
-- Persona: Data Analyst
-- Question: "What are corporate clients actually complaining about, by
--            scheme and by relationship manager - without reading 2,000 comments?"
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql (for STG_* views), or DE1
-- All functions run inside Snowflake: no data leaves the platform, no model training.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.1 Overall and aspect-based sentiment
-- AI_SENTIMENT scores the whole text and named aspects separately
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT LEFT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, 90) AS FEEDBACK,
       AI_SENTIMENT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, ['speed', 'communication', 'fees']) AS ASPECT_SENTIMENT
FROM STG_FEEDBACK
LIMIT 5;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.2 Build the enriched feedback table (score once, query many times)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FEEDBACK_ENRICHED AS
WITH ai_scored AS (
    SELECT f.*, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           -- AI_SENTIMENT returns a label, so map the overall label to -1, 0 or 1
           -- (legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT is blocked on new accounts)
           DECODE(GET(FILTER(AI_SENTIMENT(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT):categories, c -> c:name::STRING = 'overall'), 0):sentiment::STRING,
                  'positive', 1, 'negative', -1, 0)::FLOAT AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
           AI_CLASSIFY(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT,
               ['Performance Issue','Service Quality','Technical Problem',
                'Positive Experience','Feature Request']) AS CLASSIFICATION_RESULT
    FROM STG_FEEDBACK f
    LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
)
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME,
       PAYMENT_ID, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL, FEEDBACK_TEXT, PAYMENT_TYPE, RATING, SENTIMENT_SCORE,
       CASE WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE >  0.3 THEN 'POSITIVE'
            WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE < -0.3 THEN 'NEGATIVE'
            ELSE 'NEUTRAL' END                  AS SENTIMENT_LABEL,
       CLASSIFICATION_RESULT:labels[0]::STRING  AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM ai_scored;

SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS FEEDBACK,
       ROUND(AVG(SENTIMENT_SCORE), 3) AS AVG_SENTIMENT,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE') / COUNT(*) * 100, 1) AS NEGATIVE_PCT
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE ORDER BY AVG_SENTIMENT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.3 AI_FILTER: natural-language WHERE clause
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE, LEFT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, 120) AS FEEDBACK
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE'
  AND AI_FILTER(PROMPT('Does the client in this feedback explicitly state that they will or may leave the bank, move their business to another bank, review other banking providers, or tender their banking? Complaints without a stated intention to leave do not count. Feedback: {0}', FEEDBACK_TEXT))
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.4 AI_AGG: themes across many rows, per relationship manager
-- One LLM summary per group - no row limit, no prompt stuffing
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES AS
SELECT RM_NAME,
       COUNT(*) AS NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK,
       AI_AGG(FEEDBACK_TEXT,
              'You are briefing a corporate banking relationship manager. List the top 3 recurring complaint themes in this client feedback, each with a one-line recommended action. Be concise.') AS TOP_THEMES
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE' AND RM_NAME IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY RM_NAME;

SELECT RM_NAME, NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK, TOP_THEMES FROM RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES ORDER BY NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.5 AI_COMPLETE: draft a client-ready response for the worst item
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, FEEDBACK_TEXT,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5',
         'Draft a short, professional reply from a UK corporate bank to this client feedback. Acknowledge the issue, avoid admitting liability, offer a follow-up call. Feedback: ' || FEEDBACK_TEXT) AS DRAFT_REPLY
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE'
ORDER BY SENTIMENT_SCORE
LIMIT 1;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.6 Cortex Code prompts
--  "Using FEEDBACK_ENRICHED, show me which customer sectors have worsening
--   sentiment month over month and chart it."
--  "Use AI_EXTRACT on FEEDBACK_TEXT to pull out any payment reference or amount
--   mentioned, into a new table FEEDBACK_ENTITIES."
-- -----------------------------------------------------

SELECT 'DA2 complete' AS STATUS;

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA3: BRANCH NETWORK AND CATCHMENT ANALYSIS   (~45 min)
-- Persona:  Data Analyst (Retail Banking)
-- Question: "Which branches could we consolidate, who absorbs their
--            customers, and how much longer would those customers travel?"
-- Prereq:   C1 only. Uses BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL (setup/07_retail_geo_seed.sql),
--           including real road-network travel times and catchments that were
--           precomputed with OpenRouteService on Snowpark Container Services.
-- In the lab you build this in a Workspace Notebook (da3_branch_network)
-- with Cortex Code; this file is the reference SQL for each cell.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.1 Map the network (notebook: SQL cell + altair map of LON/LAT)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT 'BRANCH' AS KIND, BRANCH_NAME AS NAME, CITY, LAT, LON FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES
UNION ALL
SELECT 'ATM', ATM_ID, NULL, LAT, LON FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.ATMS WHERE SITE_TYPE = 'STANDALONE';

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.2 Drive-time catchments: who lives within a 10 and 20 minute drive
-- of each branch (ORS isochrones + ST_WITHIN)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT b.BRANCH_NAME, b.CITY, i.MINUTES,
       ROUND(ANY_VALUE(ST_AREA(i.CATCHMENT)) / 1e6, 1) AS CATCHMENT_KM2,
       COUNT(c.CUSTOMER_ID) AS CUSTOMERS_IN_CATCHMENT
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES i
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b USING (BRANCH_ID)
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
  ON c.CITY = b.CITY AND ST_WITHIN(c.HOME_LOCATION, i.CATCHMENT)
WHERE i.PROFILE = 'driving-car'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY b.CITY, b.BRANCH_NAME, i.MINUTES;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.3 Nearest branch by real drive time: each customer's fastest and
-- second-fastest branch from the ORS matrix (by the customer's H3 cell)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH AS
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, t.BRANCH_ID, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS DRIVE_MIN, t.DISTANCE_M / 1000 AS DRIVE_KM,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CUSTOMER_ID ORDER BY t.DURATION_S) AS RN
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
    JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t
      ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.PROFILE = 'driving-car'
    JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b ON b.BRANCH_ID = t.BRANCH_ID AND b.CITY = c.CITY
    QUALIFY RN <= 2
),
walk AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, MIN(t.DURATION_S) / 60 AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
    JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.PROFILE = 'foot-walking'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CITY, c.AGE_BAND, c.SEGMENT, c.DIGITAL_ACTIVE,
       MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.BRANCH_ID, NULL))          AS NEAREST_BRANCH_ID,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.DRIVE_MIN, NULL)), 1) AS NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.DRIVE_KM, NULL)), 2)  AS NEAREST_DRIVE_KM,
       MAX(IFF(r.RN = 2, r.BRANCH_ID, NULL))          AS SECOND_BRANCH_ID,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 2, r.DRIVE_MIN, NULL)), 1) AS SECOND_DRIVE_MIN,
       ROUND(ANY_VALUE(w.NEAREST_WALK_MIN), 1)        AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
JOIN ranked r USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
LEFT JOIN walk w USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CITY, c.AGE_BAND, c.SEGMENT, c.DIGITAL_ACTIVE;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.4 Overlapping catchments: branch pairs whose 10 minute drive
-- catchments overlap most (ST_INTERSECTION of the isochrones)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT * FROM (
SELECT a.CITY, a.BRANCH_NAME AS BRANCH_A, b.BRANCH_NAME AS BRANCH_B,
       ROUND(ST_DISTANCE(a.LOCATION, b.LOCATION) / 1000, 2) AS STRAIGHT_LINE_KM,
       ROUND(ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(ia.CATCHMENT, ib.CATCHMENT)) / LEAST(ST_AREA(ia.CATCHMENT), ST_AREA(ib.CATCHMENT)) * 100) AS OVERLAP_PCT
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES a
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b ON a.CITY = b.CITY AND a.BRANCH_ID < b.BRANCH_ID
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES ia ON ia.BRANCH_ID = a.BRANCH_ID AND ia.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND ia.MINUTES = 10
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES ib ON ib.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID AND ib.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND ib.MINUTES = 10
) WHERE OVERLAP_PCT >= 80
ORDER BY OVERLAP_PCT DESC, STRAIGHT_LINE_KM;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.5 Customer density with H3 (resolution 8, ~0.7 km2 cells)
-- notebook: altair heat map of cells (H3_CELL_TO_POINT gives the centre)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT HOME_H3_CELL AS H3_CELL,
       ST_Y(H3_CELL_TO_POINT(HOME_H3_CELL)) AS LAT, ST_X(H3_CELL_TO_POINT(HOME_H3_CELL)) AS LON,
       ANY_VALUE(CITY) AS CITY, COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY CUSTOMERS DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.6 Closure impact: if a branch closes, its customers move to their
-- second-fastest branch. Added drive time, lost walk-in access, cost saved.
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT AS
WITH visits AS (
    SELECT BRANCH_ID, COUNT(*) AS VISITS_12M FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_VISITS GROUP BY 1
),
walk_after AS (
    -- walking time to the receiving branch for each customer
    SELECT n.CUSTOMER_ID, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS WALK_MIN_AFTER
    FROM CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH n
    JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
    JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t
      ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.BRANCH_ID = n.SECOND_BRANCH_ID AND t.PROFILE = 'foot-walking'
),
moved AS (
    SELECT n.NEAREST_BRANCH_ID AS BRANCH_ID,
           COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS,
           ROUND(AVG(n.SECOND_DRIVE_MIN - n.NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN), 1) AS AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
           ROUND(APPROX_PERCENTILE(n.SECOND_DRIVE_MIN - n.NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN, 0.9), 1) AS P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
           COUNT_IF(n.NEAREST_WALK_MIN <= 15 AND COALESCE(w.WALK_MIN_AFTER, 999) > 15) AS LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS,
           COUNT_IF(NOT n.DIGITAL_ACTIVE OR n.AGE_BAND = '75+') AS VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS,
           MODE(n.SECOND_BRANCH_ID) AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH_ID
    FROM CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH n
    LEFT JOIN walk_after w USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.BRANCH_ID, b.BRANCH_NAME, b.CITY, b.FORMAT, b.ANNUAL_COST_GBP AS ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP,
       COALESCE(v.VISITS_12M, 0) AS VISITS_12M,
       ROUND(b.ANNUAL_COST_GBP / NULLIF(v.VISITS_12M, 0), 2) AS COST_PER_VISIT_GBP,
       m.CUSTOMERS AS CUSTOMERS_AFFECTED, m.AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN, m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       m.LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS, m.VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS, r.BRANCH_NAME AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH,
       CASE WHEN m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN >= 10 OR m.VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS >= 200 THEN 'HIGH'
            WHEN m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN >= 4 OR m.LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS >= 100 THEN 'MEDIUM' ELSE 'LOW' END AS DISRUPTION_RISK
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b
JOIN moved m ON m.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID
LEFT JOIN visits v ON v.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES r ON r.BRANCH_ID = m.MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH_ID;

SELECT BRANCH_NAME, CITY, ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP, COST_PER_VISIT_GBP, AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN, P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS, VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS, DISRUPTION_RISK, MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH
FROM BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT
ORDER BY DISRUPTION_RISK = 'LOW' DESC, COST_PER_VISIT_GBP DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.7 Semantic view for Cortex Analyst (drive minutes, no GEOGRAPHY)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  TABLES (
    closures AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT
      PRIMARY KEY (BRANCH_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('branches', 'branch closures', 'consolidation candidates')
      COMMENT = 'One row per branch: what happens if it closes',
    customers AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('retail customers', 'catchment')
      COMMENT = 'Each retail customer with their fastest and second-fastest branch by drive time'
  )
  RELATIONSHIPS (
    customers (NEAREST_BRANCH_ID) REFERENCES closures
  )
  FACTS (
    closures.annual_saving_gbp AS ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP COMMENT = 'Annual running cost saved if the branch closes (GBP)',
    closures.visits_12m AS VISITS_12M COMMENT = 'Branch visits in the last 12 months',
    closures.cost_per_visit_gbp AS COST_PER_VISIT_GBP COMMENT = 'Annual cost divided by visits',
    closures.avg_added_drive_min AS AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN WITH SYNONYMS = ('extra travel time') COMMENT = 'Average extra drive minutes to the next-fastest branch (OpenRouteService)',
    closures.p90_added_drive_min AS P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN COMMENT = '90th percentile extra drive minutes',
    closures.lose_walk_in_access AS LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS COMMENT = 'Customers who lose a branch within a 15 minute walk',
    closures.vulnerable_customers AS VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS COMMENT = 'Affected customers who are 75+ or not digitally active',
    customers.nearest_drive_min AS NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN COMMENT = 'Drive minutes from home to the fastest branch',
    customers.nearest_walk_min AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN COMMENT = 'Walking minutes from home to the nearest branch'
  )
  DIMENSIONS (
    closures.branch_name AS BRANCH_NAME WITH SYNONYMS = ('branch') COMMENT = 'Branch name',
    closures.city AS CITY COMMENT = 'City',
    closures.format AS FORMAT COMMENT = 'FULL or EXPRESS branch',
    closures.disruption_risk AS DISRUPTION_RISK COMMENT = 'LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH service disruption if closed',
    closures.main_receiving_branch AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH COMMENT = 'Branch that absorbs most customers',
    customers.age_band AS AGE_BAND COMMENT = 'Customer age band',
    customers.segment AS SEGMENT COMMENT = 'MASS, AFFLUENT or SMALL_BUSINESS',
    customers.digital_active AS DIGITAL_ACTIVE COMMENT = 'Customer uses digital banking'
  )
  METRICS (
    closures.total_saving_gbp AS SUM(closures.annual_saving_gbp) COMMENT = 'Total annual saving (GBP)',
    closures.branch_count AS COUNT(closures.branch_name) COMMENT = 'Number of branches',
    customers.customer_count AS COUNT(customers.customer_id) COMMENT = 'Number of customers',
    customers.avg_drive_min AS ROUND(AVG(customers.nearest_drive_min), 1) COMMENT = 'Average drive minutes to the fastest branch'
  )
  COMMENT = 'DA3 retail branch network and consolidation impact (OpenRouteService travel times)';

SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  METRICS closures.total_saving_gbp, closures.branch_count
  DIMENSIONS closures.city, closures.disruption_risk)
ORDER BY CITY, DISRUPTION_RISK;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.8 Branch network agent (in the lab: + > Agent > Create with CoCo)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_NETWORK_ADVISOR
  COMMENT = 'DA3: retail branch consolidation advisor'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Branch Network Advisor", "color": "orange"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto
  instructions:
    response: >
      You advise a UK retail bank on its branch network. For a consolidation question, return:
      a ranked list of candidate branches with annual saving and cost per visit, the branch that
      absorbs their customers and the added drive time (average and p90 minutes), customers who
      lose walk-in access, the disruption risk and vulnerable customers affected, and a short
      90-day transition plan. Never recommend closing a HIGH disruption-risk branch without
      saying why and what mitigation is needed.
    orchestration: "Use the Analyst tool for every question about branches, closures, catchments, travel time and customers."
    sample_questions:
      - question: "What is the consolidation opportunity in Leeds?"
      - question: "Which 3 branches could close with the least added travel time?"
      - question: "Which branch would be hardest to close, and why?"
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: "cortex_analyst_text_to_sql"
        name: "Analyst"
        description: "Retail branch network: closure impact per branch (saving, visits, added drive time, lost walk-in access, disruption risk) and customer catchments."
  tool_resources:
    Analyst:
      semantic_view: "BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_BRANCH_NETWORK"
      execution_environment:
        type: "warehouse"
        warehouse: "BARCLAYS_WH"
  $$;

SELECT 'DA3 complete' AS STATUS;

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE OPS1: CORPORATE PAYMENTS 360 AGENT   (~45 min)
-- Persona: Payments Operations analyst (no SQL needed after setup)
-- Question: "Before I call a client, tell me everything: payments health,
--            open incidents, and what they have been complaining about."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql + DA1 (SV_CLIENT_360)
--           + setup/catchup/semantic_view_and_agent.sql (SV_PAYMENTS)
--           Facilitator shortcut: run all three catch-up/DA1 scripts in order.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS1.1 The agent: two semantic views as tools + charting
-- Created in SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS so it appears in Snowflake CoWork
-- for everyone with access.
-- (Snowsight alternative: AI & ML > Agents > Create agent - same settings.)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360
  COMMENT = 'Barclays HOL - Corporate Payments 360: client payments health, incidents and sentiment'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Corporate Payments 360", "color": "blue"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto

  orchestration:
    budget:
      seconds: 90
      tokens: 20000

  instructions:
    response: >
      You support Payments Operations and Relationship Managers in a UK corporate bank.
      Lead with a one-line summary, then the supporting numbers.
      Format money in GBP with thousands separators and percentages to 1 decimal place.
      When briefing on a client, always cover: payment volume and success rate,
      failed value, open and critical alerts, and feedback sentiment with the main topic.
      If the data cannot answer the question, say so - never guess.
    orchestration: >
      Use Client360 for anything about a specific client, relationship manager,
      KYC status, alerts or incidents, and client feedback.
      Use PaymentsOps for scheme-level and daily trends: volumes by scheme/region/channel,
      processing times, P95 latency and SLA compliance or breaches.
      For a client briefing you may need Client360 more than once.
    sample_questions:
      - question: "Brief me on the client with the most failed payment value"
      - question: "Which relationship managers have the most open critical alerts?"
      - question: "Which payment schemes breached SLA most often in the last 30 days?"
      - question: "Show weekly payment volume for CHAPS as a chart"

  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: Client360
        description: >
          Corporate client 360: one row per client with sector, country, KYC status and RM;
          payment totals, success rate and failed value per client; AI-scored feedback
          sentiment and topic; and operational alerts with severity, status and resolution time.
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: PaymentsOps
        description: >
          Daily payment KPIs by scheme (CHAPS, Faster Payments, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, Wire),
          region, channel, sector and RM, plus daily SLA compliance status per scheme.
    - tool_spec:
        type: data_to_chart
        name: data_to_chart
        description: Generates charts from query results

  tool_resources:
    Client360:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_CLIENT_360
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
    PaymentsOps:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_PAYMENTS
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
  $$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS1.2 Use it - Snowflake CoWork (formerly Snowflake Intelligence)
-- Select "Corporate Payments 360" and try:
--   1. "Brief me on the client with the most failed payment value"
--   2. "Which of Priya Sharma's clients have open critical alerts?"
--   3. "Is SWIFT meeting its SLA this month? Show a chart."
--   4. "Which clients have negative sentiment AND a success rate below 96%?"
-- Expand "Show details" on each answer to see the tool and SQL used.
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- OPS1.3 The same agent from SQL (e.g. embedding in a process or app)
SELECT SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.DATA_AGENT_RUN(
  'SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360',
  $${"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Which relationship managers have the most open critical alerts?"}]}]}$$
) AS RESPONSE;

-- sees what their role is granted (see GOV1 for masking and row access).

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE OPS2: ALERT TRIAGE + NEGATIVE SENTIMENT FEED   (~30 min)
-- Persona: Payments Operations analyst / team lead
-- Question: "Which open alerts should my team work first, what should we do,
--            and which unhappy clients are linked to them?"
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql (FEEDBACK_ENRICHED, STG_* views)
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.1 Live negative-sentiment feed for the CX escalation queue
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_NEGATIVE_SENTIMENT_FEED
    TARGET_LAG = '5 minutes'
    WAREHOUSE  = BARCLAYS_WH
AS
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR,
       RM_NAME, PAYMENT_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE, FEEDBACK_TEXT, SENTIMENT_SCORE, TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE';

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.2 Prioritised triage queue: open alerts, scored for urgency
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE AS
SELECT al.ALERT_ID, al.ALERT_TIME, al.SEVERITY, al.STATUS, al.ASSIGNED_TO,
       al.PAYMENT_TYPE, al.ALERT_DESCRIPTION,
       p.PAYMENT_ID, p.AMOUNT, p.CURRENCY, p.STATUS AS PAYMENT_STATUS,
       e.ERROR_CODE, e.ERROR_DESCRIPTION, e.ERROR_CATEGORY, e.IS_RETRYABLE,
       c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.RM_NAME,
       COUNT(n.FEEDBACK_ID) AS CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK,
       -- simple, explainable priority score
       DECODE(al.SEVERITY, 'CRITICAL', 40, 'HIGH', 25, 'MEDIUM', 10, 0)
         + IFF(p.AMOUNT >= 1000000, 30, IFF(p.AMOUNT >= 100000, 15, 0))
         + LEAST(COUNT(n.FEEDBACK_ID), 20)
         + IFF(e.ERROR_CATEGORY = 'COMPLIANCE', 10, 0)        AS PRIORITY_SCORE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
JOIN STG_PAYMENTS p          ON al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ERROR_CODES e ON p.ERROR_CODE = e.ERROR_CODE
LEFT JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS a     ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c    ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN DT_NEGATIVE_SENTIMENT_FEED n ON n.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE al.STATUS <> 'RESOLVED'
GROUP BY ALL;

SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, PAYMENT_TYPE, AMOUNT, ERROR_DESCRIPTION, CUSTOMER_NAME,
       CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK, PRIORITY_SCORE
FROM V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE
ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.3 AI-recommended next action for the top of the queue
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ALERT_RECOMMENDATIONS AS
SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, PAYMENT_TYPE, CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PRIORITY_SCORE,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5',
         'You are a senior payments operations analyst at a UK bank. In at most 3 short bullet points, '
         || 'give the next actions for this alert, including whether to retry the payment and whether to contact the client or their RM. '
         || 'Alert: ' || ALERT_DESCRIPTION
         || ' | Scheme: ' || PAYMENT_TYPE
         || ' | Error: ' || COALESCE(ERROR_DESCRIPTION, 'none') || ' (' || COALESCE(ERROR_CATEGORY, 'n/a')
         || ', retryable=' || COALESCE(IS_RETRYABLE::STRING, 'unknown') || ')'
         || ' | Amount: ' || AMOUNT || ' ' || CURRENCY
         || ' | Client negative feedback items: ' || CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK) AS RECOMMENDED_ACTION
FROM V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE
ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, CUSTOMER_NAME, RECOMMENDED_ACTION
FROM ALERT_RECOMMENDATIONS ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.4 Hand it to the business
--  * Add V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE to SV_CLIENT_360 (ask CoCo to extend DA1's view), or
--  * Open payments-dashboard/ (Streamlit) and ask CoCo:
--    "Add a 'Triage' page to the Streamlit app that shows V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE
--     ordered by PRIORITY_SCORE with ALERT_RECOMMENDATIONS alongside."
-- -----------------------------------------------------

SELECT 'OPS2 complete' AS STATUS;

-- =====================================================
-- OPS3: Payments operations in Snowflake CoWork - reference SQL
-- OPS3 is done in the CoWork UI and a Workspace dashboard; this is the SQL behind it.
-- The agent and semantic view are built at provisioning (setup/09_cowork_pack.sql).
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- 1. The agent CoWork lists, and its tools (Analyst + code execution)
SHOW AGENTS IN SCHEMA SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS;
DESCRIBE AGENT SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_OPS_COWORK;

-- 2. The semantic view it answers from
SHOW SEMANTIC METRICS IN BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.SV_PAYMENTS_OPS;

-- 3. The same numbers as the chart step: monthly failed value by scheme, last 12 months
SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(
    BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.SV_PAYMENTS_OPS
    DIMENSIONS payments.payment_month, payments.payment_type
    METRICS payments.failed_value
    WHERE payments.payment_month >= DATEADD('month', -12, DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE()))
)
ORDER BY PAYMENT_MONTH, PAYMENT_TYPE;

-- 4. The Logistics story behind the Deep Research step: feedback that mentions leaving, by sector,
--    and the sector's payment failure rate (which isn't unusual - the issue is service, not failures)
WITH feedback AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_SECTOR,
           COUNT_IF(FEEDBACK_MONTH >= DATEADD('month', -4, DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE()))) AS RECENT_FEEDBACK,
           COUNT_IF(FEEDBACK_TEXT ILIKE ANY ('%other banking providers%', '%another bank%', '%tender%')) AS CHURN_MENTIONS
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.CLIENT_FEEDBACK
    GROUP BY 1
), payments AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_SECTOR, ROUND(COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'FAILED') / COUNT(*) * 100, 1) AS FAILURE_RATE_PCT
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
    WHERE PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -4, CURRENT_DATE())
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT f.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, f.RECENT_FEEDBACK, f.CHURN_MENTIONS, p.FAILURE_RATE_PCT
FROM feedback f LEFT JOIN payments p USING (CUSTOMER_SECTOR)
ORDER BY f.CHURN_MENTIONS DESC, f.CUSTOMER_SECTOR;

-- 5. The automation step's question: top 5 clients by failed value last week
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE AS MAIN_FAILING_SCHEME, FAILED_VALUE
FROM (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE,
           SUM(SUM(AMOUNT)) OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_NAME) AS CLIENT_FAILED_VALUE,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_NAME ORDER BY SUM(AMOUNT) DESC) AS RN
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
    WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED'
      AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('week', -1, DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE()))
      AND PAYMENT_DATE <  DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE())
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
WHERE RN = 1
ORDER BY CLIENT_FAILED_VALUE DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- 6. Dashboard tile queries (what Cortex Code should generate for payments_ops)
--    Scorecards
SELECT SUM(AMOUNT) AS PAYMENT_VALUE,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'COMPLETED') / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 1) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
       SUM(IFF(STATUS = 'FAILED', AMOUNT, 0)) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE());
--    Top 10 clients by failed value
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE())
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY FAILED_VALUE DESC
LIMIT 10;
--    Failed payments by error code
SELECT ERROR_CODE, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE())
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY FAILED_PAYMENTS DESC;

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE AI1: AGENT WITH CUSTOM TOOLS   (~45 min)
-- Persona: AI Builder
-- Question: "Ops staff ask about specific payments by ID and about scheme
--            rules - not just aggregates. Give the agent precise tools."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql + setup/catchup/semantic_view_and_agent.sql
-- Builds:   2 UDF tools + PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR agent
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.1 Tool 1: exact payment lookup (deterministic - no text-to-SQL guessing)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION GET_PAYMENT_DETAILS(PAYMENT_ID_IN VARCHAR)
RETURNS TABLE (PAYMENT_ID VARCHAR, PAYMENT_DATE TIMESTAMP, PAYMENT_TYPE VARCHAR,
               AMOUNT NUMBER(15,2), CURRENCY VARCHAR, STATUS VARCHAR,
               PROCESSING_TIME_MS NUMBER, ERROR_CODE VARCHAR, ERROR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR,
               IS_RETRYABLE BOOLEAN, CUSTOMER_NAME VARCHAR, RM_NAME VARCHAR,
               OPEN_ALERTS NUMBER)
COMMENT = 'Look up one payment by PAYMENT_ID with its error, client, RM and open alert count'
AS
$$
    SELECT p.PAYMENT_ID, p.PAYMENT_DATE, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.AMOUNT, p.CURRENCY, p.STATUS,
           p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS, p.ERROR_CODE, e.ERROR_DESCRIPTION, e.IS_RETRYABLE,
           c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.RM_NAME,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
             WHERE al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID AND al.STATUS <> 'RESOLVED')
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_PAYMENTS p
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ERROR_CODES e  ON p.ERROR_CODE = e.ERROR_CODE
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_ACCOUNTS a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
    WHERE p.PAYMENT_ID = UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_ID_IN))
$$;

-- Agent custom tools need a scalar return - wrap the table function as JSON
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION PAYMENT_LOOKUP(PAYMENT_ID VARCHAR)
RETURNS VARIANT
COMMENT = 'Agent tool: payment details as JSON'
AS
$$
    SELECT COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(*))[0],
                    OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('error', 'No payment found with ID ' || PAYMENT_ID))
    FROM TABLE(GET_PAYMENT_DETAILS(PAYMENT_ID))
$$;

SELECT PAYMENT_LOOKUP((SELECT MIN(PAYMENT_ID) FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED')) AS RESULT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.2 Tool 2: scheme rules ("can I still send this today?")
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION SCHEME_RULES(SCHEME VARCHAR)
RETURNS VARIANT
COMMENT = 'Agent tool: payment scheme rules - settlement cycle, value limit, cutoff and SLA'
AS
$$
    SELECT COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(
               'scheme', s.SCHEME_CODE, 'name', s.SCHEME_NAME,
               'settlement_cycle', s.SETTLEMENT_CYCLE, 'domestic', s.IS_DOMESTIC,
               'max_value_gbp', s.MAX_VALUE_GBP, 'cutoff_time_uk', s.CUTOFF_TIME::STRING,
               'currency', s.OPERATING_CURRENCY,
               'sla_target_success_rate', sla.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE,
               'sla_max_p95_ms', sla.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS))[0],
             OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('error', 'Unknown scheme. Valid: CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, WIRE_TRANSFER'))
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENT_SCHEMES s
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS sla ON sla.PAYMENT_TYPE = s.SCHEME_CODE
    WHERE s.SCHEME_CODE = UPPER(REPLACE(TRIM(SCHEME), ' ', '_'))
$$;

SELECT SCHEME_RULES('chaps') AS RESULT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.3 The agent: Analyst for aggregates + custom tools for precision
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR
  COMMENT = 'Barclays HOL - investigates individual payments and scheme rules, plus KPI questions'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Payments Investigator", "color": "green"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto
  instructions:
    response: >
      You help payments operations investigate individual payments. Be precise and brief.
      When reporting a payment, state status, error and whether it is retryable first.
    orchestration: >
      If the user gives a payment ID (format PAY followed by digits), call PaymentLookup.
      For questions about a scheme's cutoff, limit, settlement cycle or SLA, call SchemeRules.
      For counts, volumes, trends or comparisons, use PaymentsOps.
      You can chain tools, e.g. look up a payment then check its scheme's cutoff.
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: generic
        name: PaymentLookup
        description: Returns full details for a single payment ID, including error, retryability, client, RM and open alerts.
        input_schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            payment_id:
              type: string
              description: The payment ID, e.g. PAY0000000123
          required: [payment_id]
    - tool_spec:
        type: generic
        name: SchemeRules
        description: Returns rules for a payment scheme - settlement cycle, max value, daily cutoff time and SLA targets.
        input_schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            scheme:
              type: string
              description: One of CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, WIRE_TRANSFER
          required: [scheme]
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: PaymentsOps
        description: Aggregated daily payment KPIs and SLA compliance by scheme, region, channel, sector and RM.
  tool_resources:
    PaymentLookup:
      type: function

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE AI2: SNOWFLAKE-MANAGED MCP SERVER   (~30 min)
-- Persona: AI Builder
-- Question: "Our teams use different AI clients (Cortex Code, Claude, Copilot,
--            in-house apps). Expose governed payments tools to all of them once."
-- Prereq:   DA1 (SV_CLIENT_360), OPS1 (CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360), AI1 (PAYMENT_LOOKUP)
--           and the Marketplace knowledge extension installed by facilitator setup.

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI2.1 One server, four governed tools. No infrastructure to host.
-- Every call runs as the calling user's role - RBAC, masking and row
-- access policies all still apply.
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE MCP SERVER PAYMENTS_MCP
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - name: "client-360-analyst"
        type: "CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE"
        identifier: "BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_CLIENT_360"
        title: "Corporate Client 360"
        description: "Ask natural-language questions about corporate clients: payment volumes, success rates, failed value, alerts and feedback sentiment."

      - name: "payments-360-agent"
        type: "CORTEX_AGENT_RUN"
        identifier: "SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360"
        title: "Corporate Payments 360 Agent"
        description: "Full client briefings combining client 360 and scheme-level payments operations data."
        annotations:
          readOnlyHint: true
          openWorldHint: false

      - name: "payment-lookup"
        type: "GENERIC"
        identifier: "BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS.PAYMENT_LOOKUP"
        title: "Payment Lookup"
        description: "Returns full details for one payment ID: status, error, retryability, client, RM and open alerts."
        annotations:
          readOnlyHint: true
          destructiveHint: false
          idempotentHint: true
          openWorldHint: false
        config:
          type: "function"
          warehouse: "BARCLAYS_WH"
          input_schema:
            type: "object"
            properties:
              payment_id:
                description: "Payment ID, e.g. PAY0000000123"
                type: "string"

      - name: "snowflake-docs"
        type: "CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY"
        identifier: "SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_CKE.SHARED.CKE_SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_SERVICE"
        title: "Snowflake Documentation (Knowledge Extension)"
        description: "Search official Snowflake documentation. Provider-hosted Marketplace Knowledge Extension - no internal data is indexed."
  $$;

SHOW MCP SERVERS IN SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS;
DESCRIBE MCP SERVER PAYMENTS_MCP;

-- Endpoint:
--   https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/BARCLAYS_HOL/schemas/AGENTS/mcp-servers/PAYMENTS_MCP
